title: Rushls
description: Ingest, output health, viewer delivery, retention, and hooks for Rushls origins. Scrape both /metrics and /metrics/streams.

list.name: node_label
list.label: Node label
list.description: The label that tells origins apart: `instance` for static targets, `pod` for Kubernetes service discovery, `k8s_pod_name` for OpenTelemetry.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: Scrape jobs. Scraping /metrics and /metrics/streams as two jobs is common; keep both selected.

panels.title: Live streams
panels.description: Streams with an active publisher.

panels.title: Viewer connections
panels.description: Open HTTP connections from players, CDNs, and scrapers.

panels.title: Ingest
panels.description: Media payload received from publishers, excluding transport overhead.

panels.title: Egress
panels.description: HTTP body bytes handed to the network stack for playlists, media, and operator paths.

panels.title: Memory budget used
panels.description: Retained media in memory as a share of the memory budget. New streams are refused when it is full.

panels.title: Late renditions
panels.description: Renditions past their output deadline right now. Above zero, viewers are waiting for media that has not been published.

panels.title: Session failures
panels.description: Publisher sessions that ended abnormally in the selected time range.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx
panels.description: Share of HTTP responses with a server error status.

panels.title: Streams
panels.description: Streams with a publisher, streams kept for DVR after their publisher left, and connected publishers.

panels.title: Ingest bitrate
panels.description: Media payload received: the total, and the ten busiest streams. A stream at zero while its publisher is connected is a stalled encoder.

panels.title: Publisher sessions
panels.description: Session lifecycle events per interval. Failures end a session abnormally; rejections are refused by admission, limits, or capacity.

panels.title: Live streams
panels.description: Streams with a publisher right now. Late is the longest any rendition has gone past its output deadline; lag is the worst rendition's drift behind real time.

targets.expr: (sum by (stream) (rate(rushls_session_source_payload_bytes_total{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}[1m])) * 8) and on (stream) (max by (stream) (rushls_stream_publisher_active{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) == 1)

count by (stream) (rushls_rendition_output_expected{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"} == 1) and on (stream) (max by (stream) (rushls_stream_publisher_active{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) == 1)

max by (stream) (rushls_rendition_output_overdue_seconds{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) and on (stream) (max by (stream) (rushls_stream_publisher_active{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) == 1)

max by (stream) (rushls_rendition_output_lag_seconds{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) and on (stream) (max by (stream) (rushls_stream_publisher_active{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) == 1)

min by (stream) (rushls_stream_retention_min_seconds{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) and on (stream) (max by (stream) (rushls_stream_publisher_active{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) == 1)

(sum by (stream) (rate(rushls_stream_http_body_bytes_total{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}[1m])) * 8) and on (stream) (max by (stream) (rushls_stream_publisher_active{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}) == 1)

panels.title: Time past output deadline
panels.description: How long the slowest rendition has gone without publishing beyond its planned interval plus tolerance. Zero is healthy; anything above means viewers are waiting.

panels.title: Output lag
panels.description: Wall-clock progress minus published media progress since each publication started. A few seconds either way is normal; steady growth means an encoder delivers slower than real time.

targets.expr: quantile(0.5, max by (stream) (rushls_rendition_output_lag_seconds{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"} and on (stream, rendition) rushls_rendition_output_expected{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"} == 1))

panels.title: Media seconds per second
panels.description: Media published per second of wall time while a publisher is connected. Steady at 1 is real time; below it, viewers drift behind.

targets.expr: quantile(0.5, min by (stream) (rate(rushls_rendition_media_published_seconds_total{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (stream, rendition) rushls_rendition_output_expected{job=~"$job", $node_label=~"$node", stream=~"$stream"} == 1))

panels.title: Output faults
panels.description: Deadline misses, advertised gaps, and timeline breaks, summed over the selected streams.

panels.title: Rendition skew
panels.description: Largest media-time difference between renditions that should advance together, against the part duration. Skew beyond one part makes rendition switches wait.

panels.title: Egress by resource
panels.description: HTTP body throughput by resource class.

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: HTTP responses per second by status code.

panels.title: Low-latency waits
panels.description: How long LL-HLS requests wait for media that is not published yet: blocking playlist reloads and preloaded parts (p95). Waiting about one part is the protocol working; much longer means output is slow.

panels.title: Egress by stream
panels.description: Viewer egress per stream, averaged over the selected time range.

panels.title: Failures by reason
panels.description: Requests that could not be served, by reason. `unknown_stream` and `unknown_resource` are usually players polling after a broadcast ended.

panels.title: HTTP capacity used
panels.description: Open connections and requests in flight as a share of their budgets (`http.max_connections`, `http.max_requests`). New ones are refused at 100%; refusals are the bars, on the right axis.

panels.title: Retained media
panels.description: Live-window and DVR media held in memory and spilled to disk. Memory budget use is in the overview.

panels.title: DVR window
panels.description: How far back viewers can seek: the shortest and longest current window across live streams.

panels.title: Publisher pipeline memory
panels.description: Accounted ingest buffers across publishers: the total, and the largest single publisher. Exhaustion ends a session.

defaults.noValue: No publishers, or a build before 0.1.0

panels.title: Storage faults
panels.description: Failed disk spills, lost recording segments, and exhausted publisher pipelines. Each one loses media or a session. The line is disk writes waiting, on the right axis.

panels.title: Hook deliveries
panels.description: Delivered events and retries per destination.

panels.title: Hook events dropped
panels.description: Events that never reached a destination, by reason. Delivery is best-effort, so drops are reported rather than retried forever.

panels.title: Hook queue
panels.description: Events waiting per destination, and requests in flight. Each destination holds 1,000 events before the oldest is dropped.

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: One row per origin. A node missing here is not being scraped.
